citations.claim: first violating step 60: controller force 163.22 exceeds fmax 59.983, body0 speed 12.63 reflects post-collision velocity
body 0 in contact with body 1 at violating step, touching_pairs gap 0.00034
step 59 controller correctly clamped, body0 speed 12.14 before collision
velocity discontinuity at collision: vx jumps -12.14 at 59 to -12.40 at 60

counterfactual.change: Increased controller fmax from 59.983 to 200 (single field) so the same force is no longer over-limit; this shows violation is due to fmax clamping being bypassed on collision step

explanation: Controller force is correctly clamped to fmax≈59.98 at steps 58-59 while chasing waypoint, but jumps to 163.22 at step 60 exactly when bodies 0 and 1 collide (touching_pairs gap 0.00034). The velocity of body 0 changes discontinuously due to collision impulse (speed 12.14->12.64 and vx -12.14->-12.40), and the controller recomputes force from the post-collision velocity error without re-applying the fmax clamp (or adds an impulse-compensation term that exceeds fmax). Substeps_in_step=15 indicates the violation occurs inside substepped integration where clamping is bypassed.
vision_note: Steps 57-59 show the red violating body and the neighboring blue body almost touching near the green waypoint in the upper left, with no other motion. At step 60 the pair visibly collides with a sudden small shift - the red body nudges down-left and the blue body up - changing from a narrow gap to apparent contact/overlap.
